chapter: Herbie Harper and Rasch's notes on Johnson
title: Herbie Harper on Johnson's character
summary: Harper says Johnson never got angry and trusted only his wife Sonny, whom he had known since 1936-37.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I'm going to include some references to J. in conversation, taped conversation with Herbie Harper. Herbie was the choreographer for Jazz Train, and he's known
J. for a long period of time. And here we go.
Yeah, he took everything in stride. I've never really ever seen J. get overexcited or angry or say a mean thing about anybody. I've never -- and I've been knowing him since 19, what, '36, '37?
He has a way of giving you an honest evaluation of a person, but doing it delicately.

Yes. Yes. As I said, we were friends from '37, and all during those years I have never seen J. take anyone into his confidence, really, truly, except Sonny. And in Sonny he seemed to have found somebody he felt at home, he could relax and let himself go, really go, which is beautiful, because they've together had a nice thing going. And I feel that through -- from and through Sonny J.'s capable of going into even better things, because she releases his artistic b_____. By her relaxing him mentally and physically he relaxed behind his mental relaxation, his creative ability would come to life more, if only his illness at present wasn't interfering.
